questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: What is the most common clinically functioning secretory pituitary adenoma?
questions.exp: Prolactinoma is the most common functioning pituitary adenoma, presenting predominantly as a microadenoma. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Match the pituitary adenoma type to its epidemiological ranking or presentation — 1) Alpha subunit of FSH secreting adenoma 2) Prolactinoma 3) GH secreting adenoma 4) ACTH secreting adenoma … A) Most common overall but clinically insignificant B) Most common functioning adenoma (microadenoma) C) Second most common functioning adenoma (acromegaly, macroadenoma) D) Third most common functioning adenoma (Cushing disease, micro > macro)
questions.exp: Alpha subunit FSH adenomas are most common overall (silent); prolactinomas are most common functioning; GH adenomas are second; ACTH adenomas are third. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Human prolactin is a single-chain polypeptide composed of ___ amino acids.
questions.exp: Prolactin is composed of 199 amino acids, whereas GH contains 191 amino acids. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Which molecular variant of circulating prolactin represents the monomeric bioactive form?
questions.exp: Microprolactin (little prolactin, 23 kDa) is the biologically active form of prolactin. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Assess the statements regarding macroprolactin: I Macroprolactin is an inactive polymer complex assessed by gel filtration chromatography. II Macroprolactin induces profound galactorrhea and hypogonadism.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.exp: Macroprolactin is an inactive form assessed by gel filtration chromatography and does not cause clinical symptoms. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: By which gestational week do lactotroph cells appear in the lateral anterior pituitary?
questions.exp: Lactotroph cells produce prolactin in the lateral pituitary and appear by the 24th week of gestation. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Which tissue is NOT recognized as an extrapituitary site of prolactin production?
questions.exp: Extrapituitary production of prolactin occurs in the CNS, placenta, and uterus, but not the adrenal cortex. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Prolactin exerts its cellular actions by binding to a transmembrane cytokine receptor that signals via the ___ pathway.
questions.exp: Prolactin signals through the JAK/STAT cytokine pathway. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: What prerequisite is required for prolactin to successfully induce and maintain lactation in breast tissue?
opts: Concurrent high pulsatile secretion of LH and FSH
Breast tissue already primed by estrogen and progesterone
questions.exp: Prolactin induces and maintains lactation in a breast already primed by estrogen and progesterone. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Match the regulatory factor to its effect on prolactin secretion — 1) Estrogen 2) Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) 3) Dopamine (PRIF) 4) REM sleep … A) Stimulates prolactin release B) Stimulates prolactin release C) Inhibits prolactin release D) Stimulates prolactin release
questions.exp: Estrogen, TRH, VIP, oxytocin, and REM sleep stimulate prolactin release; dopamine (PRIF) inhibits prolactin release. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: A 26-year-old woman undergoes polysomnography. Prolactin secretion exhibits physiological episodic nocturnal surges correlated with:
opts: Awake state immediately prior to sleep
questions.exp: Prolactin release is physiologically stimulated during REM sleep. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Identify the factor that does NOT stimulate prolactin release:
questions.exp: Dopamine is the primary prolactin inhibitory factor (PRIF); TRH, VIP, and oxytocin stimulate release. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation
questions.q: Assess the classification of pituitary adenomas by size: I Microadenomas measure less than or equal to 1 cm. II Macroadenomas measure greater than or equal to 1 cm.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Pituitary microadenomas are defined as <= 1 cm and macroadenomas as >= 1 cm. (Book p941)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Match the fasting serum prolactin range to its clinical interpretation — 1) Less than 25 ug/L 2) 25 to 40 ug/L 3) 40 to 100 ug/L 4) Greater than 200 ug/L … A) Normal reference level B) Physiological elevation (sleep, stress, chest wall stimulation) C) Drug-induced or systemic conditions D) Definite prolactinoma (rule out macroprolactin)
questions.exp: Fasting prolactin < 25 is normal, 25-40 is physiological, 40-100 is drug-induced/systemic, > 100 suggests adenoma, and > 200 confirms adenoma. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: What peak physiological prolactin level can be attained during pregnancy?
questions.exp: During pregnancy, prolactin levels rise physiologically and can reach up to 180 ug/L. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Which clinical entity is characterized by markedly elevated serum prolactin in a completely asymptomatic individual?
questions.exp: Macroprolactin presents with high measured prolactin levels while the patient remains completely asymptomatic. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: A 40-year-old male with a 4 cm giant pituitary macroadenoma has an initial serum prolactin reported as only 45 ug/L. Suspecting the Hook effect, what is the best laboratory corrective step?
opts: Assay the sample using gel filtration chromatography
Switch from chemiluminescence to high-performance liquid chromatography
Perform serial dilution of the serum sample
Precipitate the sample with polyethylene glycol
questions.exp: The hook effect occurs in giant prolactinomas where antigen excess saturates assay antibodies yielding artifactually low prolactin; 1:100 serum dilution reveals the true massive elevation. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: A prolactinoma exceeding ___ cm in maximal diameter is categorized as a giant prolactinoma.
questions.exp: A prolactinoma measuring > 4 cm is designated as a giant prolactinoma. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Which medication is NOT listed as a pharmacological cause of hyperprolactinemia?
questions.exp: Risperidone, metoclopramide, verapamil, opiates, H2 blockers, and alpha-methyldopa cause hyperprolactinemia; levothyroxine suppresses TRH and lowers prolactin. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: A 32-year-old psychiatric patient on haloperidol develops bilateral galactorrhea. D2 receptor blockade in which central nervous system pathway produces her worsening negative symptoms?
questions.exp: Conventional antipsychotics block D2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway, worsening negative symptoms, while tuberoinfundibular blockade causes galactorrhea. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Following discontinuation of an offending pharmacological agent, drug-induced hyperprolactinemia typically demonstrates a good response and normalizes within:
questions.exp: Drug-induced hyperprolactinemia shows a good response and normalizes if the offending drug is stopped for < 72 hours. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: How does primary hypothyroidism induce hyperprolactinemia?
opts: Direct thyroid hormone toxicity impairs hypothalamic dopamine release
Thyroid peroxidase autoantibodies cross-react with D2 receptors
Thyroxine clearance of renal prolactin is drastically diminished
Elevated TRH acts as a prolactin-releasing hormone on lactotrophs
questions.exp: In primary hypothyroidism, compensatory high TRH levels stimulate lactotrophs to release prolactin. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Which systemic condition is NOT a recognized cause of hyperprolactinemia?
questions.exp: Systemic causes of hyperprolactinemia include primary hypothyroidism, PCOS, CKD, and CLD; primary hyperparathyroidism does not elevate prolactin. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Assess the characteristics of prolactinomas: I Prolactinomas are the most common pituitary adenoma. II Microprolactinomas occur more frequently than macroprolactinomas.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Prolactinomas are the most common pituitary adenoma, with microprolactinomas outnumbering macroprolactinomas. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Metoclopramide induces prominent hyperprolactinemia because, unlike domperidone, it readily crosses the ___ barrier.
questions.exp: Metoclopramide crosses the blood-brain barrier to block hypothalamic/pituitary dopamine receptors. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Fasting prolactin levels, macroprolactin and hyperprolactinemia etiologies
questions.q: Match the condition to its prolactin diagnostic hallmark — 1) Macroprolactin 2) Hook effect … A) Elevated prolactin levels with completely asymptomatic patient B) Falsely low or mismatched prolactin in presence of a massive tumor
questions.exp: Macroprolactin is high but asymptomatic; the hook effect features a large tumor with discordant prolactin. (Book p942)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: What is the female-to-male ratio in patients diagnosed with microprolactinoma?
questions.exp: Microprolactinomas show a marked female preponderance with an F:M ratio of 20:1. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: Assess gender patterns in prolactinomas: I Macroprolactinomas have an equal female-to-male ratio of 1:1. II Men with prolactinoma typically present late with compressive mass effects.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Macroprolactinomas show F:M = 1:1 because men lack menstrual cues and present late with mass effects. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: Match the patient age group to its prolactinoma clinical pattern — 1) 25 to 45 years 2) Less than 20 years … A) Most common peak age of presentation B) Genetic/syndromic causes (MEN 1, McCune-Albright, Carney complex)
questions.exp: Peak incidence occurs at 25-45 years; presentations under 20 suggest MEON syndromes (MEN 1, McCune-Albright, Carney). (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: In the galactorrhea-amenorrhea complex, hyperprolactinemia suppresses the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis leading to hypogonadism and ___.
questions.exp: Elevated prolactin inhibits the HPG axis, producing hypogonadism and luteolysis. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: A 29-year-old female presents with secondary amenorrhea, milky breast discharge, and hot flushes. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) demonstrates osteopenia localized predominantly to the:
questions.exp: Hypogonadism in hyperprolactinemia leads to osteopenia and osteoporosis involving predominantly the spine. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: Why does hypogonadism in males with prolactinoma often go unnoticed until late stages?
opts: Testosterone levels are paradoxically maintained by direct adrenal stimulation
Gynaecomastia occurs in 100% of cases providing an immediate visible cue
Men do not experience bone density loss from hypogonadism
Symptoms such as loss of libido and erectile dysfunction are subtle and insidious
questions.exp: In males, hypogonadal symptoms like loss of libido and erectile dysfunction go unnoticed until mass effects emerge. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: What percentage of patients harboring a macroprolactinoma present with visual field defects?
questions.exp: In macroprolactinomas, 35% of patients have visual field defects and 45% have hypopituitarism of other axes. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: In patients with macroprolactinoma, what proportion demonstrate deficiency of other anterior pituitary hormones?
questions.exp: Deficiency of other pituitary hormones is found in 45% of macroprolactinoma patients. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: What is the confirmatory investigation of choice (IOC) for suspected prolactinoma?
opts: Basal serum prolactin measurement at 8 AM
TRH dynamic stimulation testing with serum prolactin curve
questions.exp: The confirmatory investigation of choice is Gadolinium-enhanced MRI (T1 sagittal post-contrast). (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: Assess the MRI appearance of a pituitary microadenoma: I Pre-contrast features include gland asymmetry, depression of the sellar floor, and infundibular stalk deviation. II Post-contrast imaging shows the whole normal gland enhancing except the hypointense adenoma.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Pre-contrast microadenoma signs are asymmetry, floor depression, and stalk deviation; with contrast, the normal gland enhances while the adenoma remains hypoenhancing. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: A 35-year-old male undergoes sellar MRI for bitemporal visual deficits. The coronal post-contrast sequence demonstrates a 2.5 cm heterogeneous mass composed of cystic (non-enhancing) and solid (enhancing) areas. This lesion is a:
questions.exp: Macroprolactinomas characteristically show heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement with non-enhancing cystic areas and enhancing solid components. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: Match the pituitary imaging finding on MRI to its structural entity — 1) Pre-contrast sellar floor depression and stalk deviation 2) Non-enhancing fluid compartment within macroadenoma 3) Diffuse uniform avid post-contrast enhancement … A) Microadenoma B) Cystic component C) Normal pituitary parenchyma
questions.exp: Microadenomas produce floor depression and stalk deviation; cystic components do not enhance; normal pituitary parenchyma enhances uniformly. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Prolactinoma prevalence, clinical syndrome and MRI features
questions.q: Which syndrome is NOT part of the MEON genetic complex associated with young-onset prolactinomas (< 20 years)?
questions.exp: Genetic syndromes associated with early prolactinomas include MEN 1, McCune-Albright, and Carney complex; MEN 2 is not linked to pituitary adenomas. (Book p943)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: What is the recommended initial management for a patient diagnosed with an asymptomatic pituitary microadenoma?
opts: Wait and watch with repeat MRI in 3 to 6 months
questions.exp: For asymptomatic microadenoma, management is wait and watch with repeat MRI after 3-6 months; treat only if size increases. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: What is the first-line medical drug of choice (DOC) for symptomatic prolactinomas and macroadenomas?
questions.exp: Cabergoline is the first-line medical drug of choice for prolactinomas. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: Due to its prolonged elimination half-life, cabergoline is typically initiated at a weekly dose of ___ mg twice weekly.
questions.exp: Cabergoline has an increased half-life allowing weekly dosing at 0.25 mg twice weekly. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: Which is NOT a recognized acute adverse effect of dopamine agonists such as cabergoline?
questions.exp: Dopamine agonists cause nausea, vomiting, postural hypotension, and dizziness, rather than severe hypertension. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: At cumulative cabergoline doses exceeding 2 g/week, what major cardiopulmonary toxicities can occur?
questions.exp: Cumulative cabergoline > 2 g/week (or high doses) can cause tricuspid regurgitation (valvulopathy) and lung fibrosis. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: What proportion of prolactinoma patients exhibit dopamine agonist resistance to cabergoline?
questions.exp: Dopamine agonist resistance to cabergoline occurs in 20% of patients. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with a microprolactinoma desires pregnancy. Which dopamine agonist is preferred because of its extensive safety record in gestation?
questions.exp: Bromocriptine is used in pregnancy due to extensive historical safety data. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: If a woman taking bromocriptine during pregnancy intends to breastfeed after delivery, when should the drug be discontinued?
opts: Stop at onset of active labor
questions.exp: Bromocriptine must be stopped 7 days before lactation to allow prolactin-mediated milk production. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: Match the therapeutic milestone in prolactinoma management to its expected timeframe — 1) Normalization of serum prolactin levels 2) Significant shrinkage of tumor volume … A) Within 4 weeks B) Within 3 to 6 months
questions.exp: Prolactin levels normalize within 4 weeks; tumor shrinkage is achieved by 3-6 months. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: Which condition is NOT an established indication for surgical resection of a prolactinoma?
opts: Persistent visual field defects after 1 month of medical therapy
Asymptomatic microadenoma with serum prolactin of 60 ug/L
questions.exp: Surgical indications include dopamine agonist resistance, persistent visual defects after 1 month of medical Rx, unstable apoplexy, and pregnancy unresponsive to therapy. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: What immunohistochemical proliferation marker is utilized to evaluate extremely rare malignant prolactinomas?
questions.exp: Malignant prolactinoma is very rare and identified by the Ki67 proliferation marker. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: What modality serves as the last resort for patients with refractory prolactinoma who are unfit for surgical resection?
questions.exp: Gamma Knife stereotactic radiotherapy is the last resort if the patient is unfit for surgery. (Book p944)

questions.sec: Medical, surgical and radiation management of prolactinoma
questions.q: Assess the primary goals of prolactinoma therapy: I Normalize serum prolactin and restore gonadal axis function. II Induce tumor shrinkage and normalize anterior pituitary function.
opts: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.exp: Goals of therapy are tumor shrinkage by 3-6 months, prolactin normalization by 4 weeks, pituitary function normalization, and restoration of gonadal function. (Book p944)
